question.text: Per the current National Savings Institute amendment to the Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS), what is the maximum investment limit for a single-holder account?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current National Savings Institute amendment (verified 2026-05-15), the POMIS maximum investment is Rs. 9 lakh for a single-holder account and Rs. 15 lakh for a jointly held account. The NISM X-A workbook (p.182) still cites the older Rs. 4.5 lakh single / Rs. 9 lakh joint limits and is stale on this threshold. The Trap: Rs. 4.5 lakh reflects the legacy single-holder ceiling that has since been revised upward; Rs. 15 lakh is the joint-holder limit, not the single-holder limit. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A and XVII both test POMIS limits in the retirement-income context; cite the current National Savings Institute notification for the threshold.
